\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be invariant under every permutation of its input
coordinates. For any natural number $k$ and any subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with
$|S|=k$, the total Fourier weight of $f$ at level $k$ equals $\binom{n}{k}$ times the
Fourier weight associated with $S$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be an odd natural number, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1\le k\le n$.
For majority on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, the Fourier weight at level $n-k+1$
equals $\frac{k}{n-k+1}$ times the Fourier weight at level $k$.
\end{theorem}
